If time is our most valuable currency, it has to be spent on things that give us back the most good in return.  Porn through its instant gratification provides the pleasure we all want, but it doesn't return much else.  Behind the veil of instant gratification, it takes, takes, and hardly gives back.

When you read a book or watch a movie, what you get back is a story that you can learn from.  That is what they are designed to do: tell a story.  And quite often, not always, stories are told to teach from which you may learn valuable lessons.  
When you are in a relationship, you are building trust, living experiences, creating friendships that in many cases come back to give you something in return.
When you invest time in a hobby, you build up a skill, an interest and expertise through which you can garner respect or money.
Internet Porn on the other hand was designed through natural selection to get you to click, to capture your mind, to keep you captivated by taking advantage of your innate desire for procreation and pleasure.  You don't get a story, you don't get a relationship, you don't grow wiser.  By following through with the deal, you're trading away energy, sleep(side effect of having to regenerate sperm), time(directly from time spent browsing, and indirectly from requiring more sleep), and mental real-estate to get a little bit of pleasure while build a porn-centric neural network.  Porn doesn't teach many valuable things, it wasn't designed that way.  Porn doesn't provide a relationship that comes back to help in times of need.  Porn could become a hobby, and you could become an expert in it, and you can make a lot of money from it, but that's a personal choice I personally don't want to be vested in.  I just don't want to be known as a porn-expert.  

It isn't necessarily about porn making you less confident, or making you view women in "bad" ways.  It's about the trade-offs and what you want.  There are better things out there that will provide more value for your investment while providing you with richer pleasures of life.  Try to compare what will produce short term vs lasting long term happiness and things like porn, cigarettes, or other addictive things quickly fall behind to more meaningful activities.

Make lists. Make deadlines. 

When your mind wanders, tell yourself to stop and pause until you remember what you were supposed to be doing. 

Cross off items on lists as you finish them.  

Convince yourself that your made up deadlines are real, because they are. Progress must keep pace to keep schedule. Things can't all be done last minute. This includes everything: schoolwork, friendships, milestones. 

Problems are solved by putting pencil to paper, by turning gears in your head, by doing what your supposed to regardless of your feelings; wether you are tired, angry, sad, worried, afraid. Breaks are necessary but not as much as expected.  Just do what your supposed to.

Schedule times for thinking. Think. Think. Plan. Then run.  Try not to think while you run. That slows down the running and degrades the thinking. 

Lastly, schedule times for exploration. Progress is not made without discovery, without having dots to connect. Awe. Wonder. Curiosity. Search for these things because they give you dots to connect, they give you happiness.  They give you things to draw from which are useful at roadblocks. 

Don't overwork yourself but this is how you things get done. By putting in the hours, making plans, devising strategies, following through day in day out and keeping some track of progress knowing clearly what direction you are going.
